title: Surjectivity of the symmetric-product morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $n\ge1$. Write $\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)$ and $\mathbf P^n_S=\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,n\};S)=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], with structure morphism $q_n=\mathrm{pr}_1:\mathbf P^n_S\to S$, and let $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n=\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\cdots\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$ be the $n$-fold fibre product over $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $\mathrm{pr}_i:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to\mathbf P^1_S$ and $p_n:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to S$. Let $\sigma_n:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to\mathbf P^n_S$ be the symmetric-product morphism $((x_1:y_1),\dots,(x_n:y_n))\mapsto[F_0:\cdots:F_n]$, $\prod_{i=1}^n(x_it+y_i)=\sum_{j=0}^nF_jt^j$ [def-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-morphism], constructed in [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-properties] as the morphism $\varphi_{p_n,(\mathcal L_n,(F_0,\dots,F_n))}$ [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] of the invertible module $\mathcal L_n=\mathrm{pr}_1^*\mathcal O(1)\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathrm{pr}_n^*\mathcal O(1)$ and its generating sections $F_j$ (here $x_i,y_i$ are the pullbacks along $\mathrm{pr}_i$ of the coordinate sections $T_0,T_1$ of $\mathcal O(1)$ on $\mathbf P^1_S$). Then $\sigma_n$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]: every point of $\mathbf P^n_S$ is the image of a point of $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$. (The source also said 'finite'; finiteness is the separate node [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-finite] and is not a claim of this node. The source's 'equivalently, over every algebraically closed geometric point every binary form of degree $n$ factors into $n$ linear forms, including factors at infinity' is not claimed as an equivalence: the factorization is proved in step 3 and is what the proof uses.)

proof.text: *A geometric point over $p$.* Let $p\in\mathbf P^n_S$, let $\kappa(p)$ be its residue field [def-weil-residue-field] and $K$ an algebraic closure of $\kappa(p)$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The point $p$ together with the inclusion $\kappa(p)\to K$ is a geometric point $\xi:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathbf P^n_S$ lying over $p$ [def-weil-geometric-point]: the image of the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is $p$ ($\xi$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(p)\to K)$ followed by the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(p)\to\mathbf P^n_S$, whose image is $\{p\}$; in Mathlib `Scheme.fromSpecResidueField` and `range_fromSpecResidueField`, Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ResidueField.lean:237,276). Since $\mathbf P^n_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ with $q_n=\mathrm{pr}_1$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], put $g=q_n\circ\xi:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ and $\psi=\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\xi:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$; by the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], $\xi$ is the unique morphism with these two components.

*Homogeneous coordinates of $\psi$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points] (Stacks 01NE), $\psi=\psi_{(\mathcal N,(u_0,\dots,u_n))}$ for an invertible $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$-module $\mathcal N$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and global sections $u_j$ generating it. $\operatorname{Spec}K$ has one point and $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}K,\mathcal O)=K$; an invertible module is locally free of rank one, so on the one-point space $\operatorname{Spec}K$ it is free of rank one: choosing a generator gives an isomorphism $\beta:\mathcal N\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$, and $\beta(u_j)=a_j\in K$. That the $u_j$ generate $\mathcal N$ at the unique point means that some $a_j\ne0$. Hence $(\mathcal N,(u_j))\sim(\mathcal O,(a_0,\dots,a_n))$ and $\psi=\psi_{(\mathcal O,(a_0,\dots,a_n))}$ with $(a_0,\dots,a_n)\in K^{n+1}\setminus\{0\}$ (equivalent pairs give the same morphism).

source.place: Lemma 27.13.1 (Tag 01NE, label lemma-projective-space), applied to Y = Spec K

proof.text:
*Factorization of the binary form (the content of the geometric fibre).* Claim: there are $(x_i,y_i)\in K^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}$, $i=1,\dots,n$, with $\prod_{i=1}^n(x_it+y_i)=\sum_{j=0}^na_jt^j$ in $K[t]$. Indeed $P(t)=\sum_ja_jt^j$ is nonzero (step 2); let $d\le n$ be its degree and $c=a_d
e0$ its leading coefficient. As $K$ is algebraically closed, [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization] gives $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_m\in K$ with $P=c\prod_{k=1}^m(t-\gamma_k)$; comparing degrees ($c
e0$ and the product of $m$ monic linear factors has degree $m$), $m=d$. If $d\ge1$ put $(x_1,y_1)=(c,-c\gamma_1)$, $(x_k,y_k)=(1,-\gamma_k)$ for $2\le k\le d$; if $d=0$ put $(x_1,y_1)=(0,c)$. In both cases put $(x_i,y_i)=(0,1)$ for the remaining $i\le n$ (the $n-d$ factors at infinity: the binary form $\sum_ja_jt^ju^{n-j}$ is divisible by $u^{n-d}$). Every pair is nonzero ($c
e0$), and $\prod_i(x_it+y_i)=c\prod_{k=1}^d(t-\gamma_k)\cdot1=P$.

*The lift $\eta$.* For each $i$ the sections $x_i,y_i$ of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$ generate it (step 3: not both zero, $K$ a field). Let $\eta_i=\varphi_{g,(\mathcal O,(x_i,y_i))}:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathbf P^1_S$ [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] (with index set $\{0,1\}$): so $q_1\circ\eta_i=g$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\eta_i=\psi_{(\mathcal O,(x_i,y_i))}$. Since all $\eta_i$ lie over the same $g$, the universal property of the iterated fibre product $(\mathbf P^1_S)^m=(\mathbf P^1_S)^{m-1}\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$ [def-pc-fibre-product], applied for $m=1,\dots,n$, gives a morphism $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$ with $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\eta=\eta_i$ for all $i$ and $p_n\circ\eta=g$.

*$\sigma_n\circ\eta=\xi$.* First components: $q_n\circ\sigma_n=p_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-over-base], so $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\sigma_n\circ\eta=p_n\circ\eta=g=\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\xi$. Second components: by the construction of $\sigma_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-properties], $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\sigma_n=\psi_{(\mathcal L_n,(F_j))}$, and by the compatibility of $\psi$ with pullback [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points], $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\sigma_n\circ\eta=\psi_{(\eta^*\mathcal L_n,(\eta^*F_j))}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (2), $\eta^*\mathcal L_n\cong\bigotimes_i\eta^*\mathrm{pr}_i^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\bigotimes_i(\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\eta_i)^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}}(1)$, compatibly with pullback of tensor products of sections, where $\mathcal O(1)$ on $\mathbf P^1_S$ is the pullback of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}}(1)$ along $\mathrm{pr}_2$ with sections $T_0,T_1$; and by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points] for $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\eta_i=\psi_{(\mathcal O,(x_i,y_i))}$ there is an isomorphism $(\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\eta_i)^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$ carrying $T_0,T_1$ to $x_i,y_i$. Tensoring, $\eta^*\mathcal L_n\cong\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}K}^{\otimes n}=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$, and since $F_j=\sum_{|J|=j}\prod_{i\in J}x_i\prod_{i\notin J}y_i$ (each monomial a tensor product of one of $x_i,y_i$ from each factor) [lem-weil-pbc-product-linear-forms-coefficients], $\eta^*F_j$ goes to $\sum_{|J|=j}\prod_{i\in J}x_i\prod_{i\notin J}y_i\in K$, which by the same node (with $R=K$) is the coefficient of $t^j$ in $\prod_i(x_it+y_i)$, i.e. $a_j$ by step 3. Hence $(\eta^*\mathcal L_n,(\eta^*F_j))\sim(\mathcal O,(a_j))$, so $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\sigma_n\circ\eta=\psi_{(\mathcal O,(a_j))}=\psi=\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\xi$ (step 2). By the uniqueness in the universal property of $\mathbf P^n_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-pc-fibre-product], $\sigma_n\circ\eta=\xi$.

proof.text: *Surjectivity.* Let $z\in(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$ be the image under $\eta$ of the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$. By step 5 and step 1, $\sigma_n(z)=\xi(\mathrm{pt})=p$. As $p$ was arbitrary, the underlying map of $\sigma_n$ is surjective, i.e. $\sigma_n$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. (No finiteness or finite-type hypothesis is used, and no fibre-wise criterion such as [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-nonempty-fibres] is needed: the lift is built directly over each point.)

The one-sentence blueprint proof (nonempty geometric fibres + lem-weil-pbc-surjective-nonempty-fibres) is replaced by a direct pointwise lift: for p in P^n_S, the geometric point Spec K -> P^n_S over p (K = algebraic closure of kappa(p)) has coordinates (a_j) != 0 by the functor of points (Stacks 01NE); the polynomial sum a_j t^j factors over K by the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization, padded with factors (0,1) at infinity; the pairs (x_i,y_i) give a K-point eta of (P^1_S)^n, and sigma_n o eta = xi is checked on both components of S x P^n_Z by the pullback compatibility of the functor of points, lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor and lem-weil-pbc-product-linear-forms-coefficients. lem-weil-pbc-surjective-nonempty-fibres (unit sk-thm-br, off this unit's route) and lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-finite are no longer used; def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions repointed to def-weil-surjective-morphism.
